recent_posts.title: Building a prank tool that silently corrupts git history
recent_posts.summary: A developer created a prank tool called Git Shitstorm that silently corrupts Git history by randomly inserting code changes from the repository. The tool works by aliasing the git command and acting like Russian roulette—90% of the time it does nothing, but 10% of the time it selects random files, authors, and code snippets to inject into commits. Implemented in Go for speed, it adds minimal latency (under 100ms) making it nearly undetectable. The author emphasizes this is for educational and entertainment purposes only, warning against using it maliciously on coworkers' repositories.

recent_posts.title: Cringe Chat shows how people type messages in real time
recent_posts.summary: Cringe Chat is an experimental chat application that shows exactly how people type their messages in real-time, including typos, corrections, and pauses. Built with FastAPI and WebSockets, it uses the human-replay library to capture and replay typing patterns, bringing back a sense of humanness to online interactions. The app requires knowing the other person's username to prevent abuse, and can be tested by connecting to yourself or using multiple browser windows.

recent_posts.title: Tailwind Alchemist: find all tailwind colors in your codebase
recent_posts.summary: Tailwind Alchemist is a CLI tool that scans codebases to find hardcoded Tailwind color names, helping developers migrate to semantic color systems like DaisyUI. The tool, built in TypeScript, supports Tailwind v4 and offers multiple verbosity levels to identify colors at the file, line, and class utility level. It addresses the challenge of refactoring projects that start with templates containing hardcoded colors when transitioning to theme-based design systems.

recent_posts.title: How to use sandboxed Claude with PHP
recent_posts.summary: Setting up Claude Code to run safely in a Docker sandbox with PHP and Laravel support on Manjaro Linux. The guide covers installing Docker Desktop, creating a custom Dockerfile with PHP 8.4 and extensions, configuring PostgreSQL to accept connections from Docker containers, and integrating Laravel Boost MCP server for database operations. This approach allows Claude to run autonomously without direct access to the host filesystem.

recent_posts.title: Yahoo deleted my emails without warning after account inactivity
recent_posts.summary: Yahoo deleted all emails from an inactive account without warning, despite having contact information to notify the user. The author lost decades of personal correspondence and memories from their first email address, created as a teenager. Yahoo's policy deletes all data after account deactivation due to inactivity, with no backup option or grace period, affecting many users who lost irreplaceable conversations including those with deceased friends.

recent_posts.title: Client-side encryption for web apps (4/4): Possible improvements and conclusion
recent_posts.summary: This final part of a client-side encryption series explores security improvements including using IndexedDB to store non-exportable CryptoKey objects instead of base64 strings in localStorage, preventing DEK export attacks. It discusses double-hashing passwords to avoid sending clear-text credentials to the backend, examines zero-knowledge protocols like SRP and OPAQUE, and notes bcrypt's 72-character limitation. The author acknowledges the implementation prevents database theft attacks but not XSS, MITM, or server-side logging vulnerabilities, and seeks community feedback on the approach.

recent_posts.title: Client-side encryption for web apps (2/4): Storing the salt and DEK, and encrypting/decrypting data
recent_posts.summary: This tutorial demonstrates implementing client-side encryption by storing salts on the backend and Data Encryption Keys (DEK) in localStorage. It covers generating initialization vectors (IVs) for AES-GCM encryption, converting CryptoKey objects to base64 for storage, and encrypting/decrypting data with proper IV handling. The implementation includes database schema changes to store encrypted amounts and IVs, with practical code examples for key serialization, data encryption/decryption functions, and performance considerations showing encryption takes ~0.06ms per operation.

recent_posts.title: Client-side encryption for web apps (1/4): PBKDF2, DEK and CryptoJS
recent_posts.summary: PBKDF2 can derive cryptographic keys from passwords for client-side encryption in web applications. The Web Crypto API provides methods to generate salts, wrap passwords into CryptoKey objects, and derive Data Encryption Keys (DEK) using PBKDF2 with SHA-256 and 600,000 iterations. The derived key uses AES-GCM for symmetric encryption. All crypto operations work with Uint8Array typed arrays, which can be converted to base64 strings for storage. This approach enables encrypting sensitive data in the browser before sending it to the server, preventing server-side access to plaintext values.

recent_posts.title: The beauty of goofy diagrams
recent_posts.summary: Visual presentation style significantly impacts learning effectiveness. Informal, hand-drawn diagrams can make technical content feel more accessible and reduce cognitive barriers compared to formal, polished diagrams. While both styles convey the same information, goofy or casual visual approaches create a relaxed mood that increases confidence and openness to learning. The style should match the goal: formal presentations for credibility, informal ones for teaching. Tech educators like The Primeagen successfully use hand-drawn diagrams to make complex topics approachable.

recent_posts.title: Building a pinball machine tracker with Laravel and API monitoring
recent_posts.summary: A developer built a Laravel app that monitors a pinball location API and sends notifications when machines are added or changed in their area. The system uses queued jobs with random delays to avoid API rate limits, stores historical data for tracking changes over time, and sends updates via Telegram to a private group. The project was deployed using Coolify on a Hetzner server and demonstrates how developers can quickly build personal tools that solve niche problems.
